title: spi_host: the error status bits for programming violations
conditions: After a violation of the programming model, as listed in the section "Error Interrupt Conditions".
Each setting is encoded as 1 if the statement about the design holds and 0 if it does not.

requirements.text: - If [`COMMAND`](registers.md#command) is written when [`STATUS.READY`](registers.md#status) is zero, the IP will assert [`ERROR_STATUS.CMDERR`](registers.md#error_status).
requirements.note: First of the six error events.
A write to TXDATA when the TX FIFO is full.
A read of RXDATA when the RX FIFO is empty.
A command segment with an invalid width or direction.
A command segment to an invalid CSID.
A write to the TXDATA window with an unknown data type.

requirements.text: Whenever an error event occurs, the error must be acknowledged by clearing (write 1 to clear) the corresponding bit in [`ERROR_STATUS`](registers.md#error_status).

design.note: The command queue reports an error when a command is written while it is busy.
STATUS.READY is the inverse of the same busy signal.

design.description: no field named CMDERR (ERROR_STATUS's fields are ACCESSINVAL, CSIDINVAL, CMDINVAL, UNDERFLOW, OVERFLOW and CMDBUSY)

claims.setting: writing COMMAND while STATUS.READY is 0 sets an ERROR_STATUS bit (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: ERROR_STATUS has a field named CMDERR (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

claims.setting: ERROR_STATUS has fields named OVERFLOW, UNDERFLOW, CMDINVAL, CSIDINVAL and ACCESSINVAL (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: an ERROR_STATUS bit is cleared by writing 1 to it (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

generated_from_same_input: D4 to D11 are in spi_host.hjson, from which reggen generates the register RTL and registers.md; those generated files are not counted as further evidence. D1 to D3 are in the hand-written RTL. R1 to R7 are hand-written.
finding: The six error events, the condition for the first one and the write-1-to-clear acknowledgement agree with the design. One name is wrong: writing COMMAND while STATUS.READY is 0 sets ERROR_STATUS.CMDBUSY; there is no CMDERR field.
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the RTL; it does not simulate an error. The conditions in R2 to R6 are compared by name only.
out_of_scope: That the IP halts until the error bit is cleared (line 598).
ERROR_ENABLE, which selects which errors raise the error interrupt.
